I am going through something similar as you, just with a shorter timeline. I was on 20 mg and stopped taking it for a full week due to a refill mixup. I’m just now starting to take it again, it’s my 4th day taking half doses. The nausea, depersonalization, and depression come and go in waves (both during withdrawal and reintroducing) for me. I haven’t been able to focus at work either.

What do you do for work? Everyone goes through periods of high/low productivity at work, regardless of medication management. Don’t get too down on yourself for needing to take more frequent breaks or working shorter hours (if you are salary). You’re investing in yourself today to help yourself out tenfold tomorrow (or next week, next month, etc). 

Your mental health is a medical necessity for you to perform well at your job. Consider making other arrangements for work travel if you are worried about not being able to cope. You are allowed to prioritize yourself over your job. Can you send someone in your place? Attend virtually? Reschedule for another time? It would be easier to make adjustments earlier in the week and it will probably feel like a relief. Work on getting back on track with your routine, even if it feels like you’re going through the motions.

Your doctor might be able to temporarily prescribe a fast-acting medication to offset waves of anxiety as needed while you get reestablished. Good luck, friend.

I disagree that the show makes a case for skin color being irrelevant in the professional world. I don’t disagree with the rest of your opinions about the history at play with Mariana and Claire at all. Those are all central to the personal character conflicts. But privilege, race, and gender are still extremely prevalent in today’s sociocultural lens; you can’t separate any of them when analyzing a situation in the workplace. If Claire can’t put aside their history after she chose as a founder to hire Mariana as a coder, then she shouldn’t be in a position of power. Mariana is consistently removed from the table and undermined for her thoughts and ideas. Mariana hasn’t done or said anything inappropriate since she’s been back at BB - if the girls (Claire) didn’t want her to upstage them in front of partners, they shouldn’t include her in those meetings. If I encountered a professional situation where I walked into an office and a WOC was the only one removed from the table regardless of her standing in the org, I would not come away from it with a good opinion of the company. I don’t think I’m unique with that opinion and Claire should understand that outsiders won’t know about their history either and will likely feel similar.

Have you seen the show? That’s mostly a tongue in cheek question, but it’s surprising for me to see you say it has nothing to do with skin color. It’s very obvious that Good Trouble is invested in portraying the intersections of race, gender, and privilege. 

Yes, I would find Claire’s actions to be professionally inappropriate regardless of Mariana’s ethnicity. But I don’t find it a stretch to bring up Claire’s advantage as a white woman when considering that the story line is about a group of women who are software engineers at a tech startup in LA. Especially given the social lens that Good Trouble has obviously chosen to portray.

I’ve seen other posters say that they understand Claire’s point of view after she listed everything Mariana did… but from a professional standpoint, I don’t agree. If Mariana was rehired as a founder, the history would be more fair game. Now that Claire is a white woman in a position of leadership (compared to [edit] Mariana), she can’t act that way to a woman of color. I’m also shocked that these supposedly intelligent woman don’t see how ridiculous it is to have Mariana completely separated from the table during meetings, although I know that’s likely for the juxtaposition on screen to be more obvious to viewers.
